lines.japanese: 当たり前のことだけど、グレタガルドから戻ってきても、文集制作はまったく進んでいなかった。
lines.english: Naturally, the graduation anthology had not advanced by a single line while I was in Gretagard.

lines.japanese: それどころか、完成させたインデックスのページがくしゃくしゃになっている。最悪だ。
lines.english: Worse, the index page I had already completed was crumpled beyond use. This was the worst.

lines.japanese: はあ、だからと言って放りだすわけにもいかないな。
lines.english: Haaah. Even so, I could hardly abandon the work.

lines.japanese: 僕は新しい用紙を取りだして修復にとりかかった。
lines.english: I took out a fresh sheet of paper and began reconstructing it.

lines.japanese: だけど、一度完成させたものをまた作りなおす作業は拷問に近い。昔のお坊さんは経典を作るのに、何度も何度も写経したっていうけど、それなら確かに悟りの一つも啓けそうだ。
lines.english: But recreating something once finished was very nearly torture. Monks of old were said to copy sutras again and again. Work like this might indeed bring a person to enlightenment.

lines.japanese: 僕の手はすぐに浮気をして、ふらふらと違う何かを求めて部屋の中を見回した。何かって言っても、元から部屋の中が寂しい僕のことだ。見つかるものなんて、そうそうない。
lines.english: My hands soon strayed from the task, and I began looking idly around the room for something else to do. But my room had always been a barren place. There was little hope of finding anything.

lines.japanese: パソコンの電源を入れて掲示板にでも行けば、不特定多数の無機質な文字列が、僕の愚痴でも相談でもない与太話に付き合ってくれるんだと思う。
lines.english: If I switched on the computer and visited a message board, impersonal strings of text from nameless strangers would surely humor whatever idle chatter I offered them—not quite a complaint and not quite a plea for advice.

lines.japanese: だけど、そうじゃない。肉声が、生の声が聞きたい。
lines.english: But that was not what I wanted. I wanted a voice. A living voice.

lines.japanese: ほんの一週間前までは、生の声なんて大それた希望だった。それが一度贅沢に慣れると、基準の高さが変わってしまうんだろうか。羽田鷹志も偉くなったもんだ。
lines.english: Only a week ago, wanting to hear a living voice had seemed far too much to ask. Had one taste of luxury raised my standards so quickly? Takashi Haneda had certainly risen in the world.

lines.japanese: 結局、僕が手にしていたのは携帯電話だった。誰にかけるんだろう。そんな相手も居ないっていうのに。
lines.english: In the end, I found my phone in my hand. Whom did I mean to call? There was nobody.

lines.japanese: 数分間ただ見つめてから、僕はケータイを開いて、登録メモリから「０２」を呼びだした。
lines.english: After staring at it for several minutes, I flipped the phone open and selected contact 02.

lines.japanese: 森里君。僕のたった一人の友達。通話ボタンを押すと、ぷっぷっぷっと電波を基地局に繋げる音がした。
lines.english: Morisato. My one and only friend. I pressed the call button, and three short tones sounded as the phone connected to a cell tower.

lines.japanese: 今日は繋がるかもしれない。なんとなくそんな気がした。
lines.english: Perhaps he would answer today. For no reason at all, I felt that he might.

lines.japanese: 森里君が電話に出たら、学校のことは話さないでおこう。それよりも、そうだ、最近ハマッてるプロレス技なんかの話がいい。
lines.english: If Morisato answered, I would avoid talking about school. We could discuss something else—yes, the wrestling moves he had been into lately.

lines.japanese: 僕は昔、彼にかけられたスコーピオンデスロックを思いだした。あれは苦しかったけど、僕はギブアップまで２分半も耐えたんだ。森里君は友人たちと、すげーすげーと笑ってくれた。
lines.english: I remembered the Scorpion Deathlock he had once put me in. The pain had been terrible, yet I endured for two and a half minutes before submitting. Morisato and his friends had laughed and shouted about how incredible it was.

lines.japanese: しばらく待つと、女性の声が聞こえてきた。オカケニナッタオ客様ハ電波ノ届カナイ所ニオラレルカ電源ガ入ッテオリマセン。
lines.english: After I had waited a while, a woman’s voice came through. THE PERSON YOU HAVE CALLED IS OUTSIDE THE SERVICE AREA OR HAS THEIR PHONE SWITCHED OFF.

lines.japanese: 僕は黙ってケータイの電源ボタンを押した。でもひとの声が聞けたんだから、結果としてよかったんじゃないかと思う。
lines.english: Silently, I pressed the phone’s power button. Still, I had heard a human voice. Perhaps that meant the attempt had ended well after all.

lines.japanese: 椅子を正面に向けて写経を再開した。
lines.english: I turned my chair back toward the desk and resumed copying my sutras.
